issues.title: REQ-022.md's AC-security fixture contains an invalid-hex UUID literal that cannot be inserted into a uuid column
issues.description: docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-022.md's AC-security fixture INSERTs a user row with id 'c0002200-0000-0000-0000-00000000a5o1' -- the last group contains the character 'o', which is not valid hex (0-9a-f), so `INSERT INTO users (...) VALUES ('c0002200-0000-0000-0000-00000000a5o1', ...)` fails with Postgres error 22P02 (invalid input syntax for type uuid). TEST-RUNNER substituted the semantically-identical valid-hex id 'c0002200-0000-0000-0000-00000000a501' in its own scratch harness to unblock verification (a like-for-like fixture-literal fix, not a change to the case's logic or expected outcomes) and confirmed the case passes with that substitution. Flagging so REQ-022.md's AC-security fixture can be corrected at the source before any future re-run copies the broken literal verbatim.

issues.title: REQ-022.md's AC-catalog grep count of 27 does not account for a pre-existing checkin-catalog key sharing the name usageNoId
issues.description: AC-catalog's grep pattern includes 'usageNoId', which is also the name of a pre-existing key in the checkin catalog section (apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts) unrelated to withdraw. The literal grep therefore returns 30 matches (9 withdraw keys x 3 files = 27, plus 3 incidental checkin usageNoId hits), not the spec's stated 27. TEST-RUNNER independently confirmed all 9 withdraw keys are genuinely present in all 3 files at the withdraw section's own line ranges (27/27 withdraw-specific matches), so this is a spec wording imprecision, not a real coverage gap. Flagging so REQ-022.md's AC-catalog can either scope the grep to the withdraw block or state the expected total as 30 with the extra 3 named.
